account:
Today’s unusual business is the eighteen-hundred gathering in the town hall great hall. I approved it as a half-hour appointment about civic hospitality and community gatherings, with the secretary escorting me, but the committee has not supplied its detailed agenda. The innkeeper, builder and freight appear to be organizing refreshments through the baker. The secretary reports an original order of 120 loaves, plus eighty additional loaves for which builder paid thirty-two planks. Payment for the original order remains unverified; the baker cannot confirm it, and builder referred questions to innkeeper or freight. I have authorized no treasury payment. I heard builder repeatedly offer to collect his remaining thirty-two loaves, and a townsman later reported seeing him carrying a bread sack.

Two townspeople have repeated reports connecting discussions at the bakery with a bridge or port change, naming baker, builder, freight and innkeeper. These are secondhand reports, not a confirmed proposal. My questions have often gone unheard as people moved away, so I still do not know whether transport changes are actually planned. I have asked the secretary to verify both the original bread order’s terms and whether bridge or port changes are proposed.

The refreshments and organizing suggest a substantial community gathering, but I do not yet know its actual purpose or whether anything is deliberately being kept from me. The neighbour also asked whether it was public or private and has invited me to our usual tea at three. My scheduled council-letters session has produced no correspondence: the secretary says none was delivered to the office, and none was delivered directly to me. It is now just after two, and the innkeeper has appeared outside town hall carrying a lantern. He may be able to explain the gathering directly.
